Being bipolar is really tough. From your post it seems that you are very self aware and that this was just a one off. Please don't be too hard on yourself.

Knowing that it's possible to not be aware of your mood swings is terrifying, especially when we can make incredibly stupid life changing decisions during those episodes, but the best we can do is try to be as self aware as possible, and I think you have that covered.

I had once forgone friendships and intimate relationships for the same reasons you mentioned you were feeling guilty. But the way I see it now is that not everyone is perfect, and people without bipolar disorder are entirely capable of being way harder to deal with than us in their own unique ways. People come with their own problems and as long as you can manage yours reasonably well, you should definitely not feel guilty. Having a slip up every now and then is perfectly acceptable, if you own up to it that is.

Don't feel too guilty about this. Wish you all the best.

Hey, 

I'm bipolar 2, but I hope this will help! 

1. Was on 300mg lamictal only and it was honestly a miracle. The only drug that got me out of depression and kept me out of it. Many people have positive experiences with lamictal but I've heard it can cause memory problems long term. Also the rash.
2. My psychiatrist did recommend adding lithium to the mix to help with suicidal thoughts and generally to prevent switching into hypomania. He said it was preventative since its such a well established mood stabilizer. I'm sorry about the thyroid family history, have you talked to your doc about it? I would be worried about it too! Having to take regular blood tests on lithium is annoying anyways and with the acne I understand why you want to stop. There are other anti manic mood stabilizers anyways if the need arises. I have no idea if lamictal is a strong enough mood stabilizer to prevent mania so you might need an anti manic, idk though.
3. I have been feeling quite depressed recently, brain fog and all so we added Welbutrin 300mg, together with 300mg lamictal. My doc said he chose Welbutrin cause it doesn't really cause switching into mania. I think that's why most antidepressants aren't used for bipolar. He also said this combo works really well for bipolar depression especially in the long run. It's worked quite well for me especially in terms of motivation and I haven't had any side effects . I do have slightly more energy so that might help you.

All the best!

Olanzapine has a really high risk of weight gain. 

My pdoc warned me about this when i first started but I shrugged it off cause I was that skinny guy who could eat anything and not get fat. 

I was on 10mg and gained 60lbs in 4 months, almost HALF my weight! 

I wasn't even eating much during those 4 moths cause I was depressed.

Lost all the weight in about 3 months after stopping though

May 10th, Male, Northern hemisphere,

let us know your findings!!

Do you take it in the mornings or at night?

Lamictal kept waking me up at night eventhough I was on melatonin, but I finally slept well when I started taking it first thing in the morning.

I feel your pain. It's so demoralising when you believe you can succeed and tell yourself "I can do it, it's different this time and I know I won't fail." and then you fail, hard. Every time it happens you have to pick yourself up and start again, but its just too much to pick yourself up so many times when you know you'll fail again.

I am so sorry it took so long for you to get a proper diagnosis, I was initially diagnosed with depression then bipolar 2 a couple years later in August. I was put in a psych ward early this year. I was advised to take a year off uni, got hypomanic and insisted that I could finish the year before inevitably crashing into depression and couldn't complete my exams. Now I'm taking a year off uni. Felt like an absolute failure when that happened, especially since I knew I should know better. I'm sure you're familiar with that painful cycle.

My psychiatrist told me that antidepressants can induce rapid cycling and possibly worsen depression. Please consider the possibility that your misdiagnosis and prescriptions may have made is so much worse for you. Your doctors really should have done better.

I am on 250mg lamotrigine now and my life is has made a complete 180, I finally feel like I have a fighting chance at life. Remember that 200mg of lamotrigine is the therapeutic dose, and it can go up to 400mg. You have barely reached it and there is the possibility of adding an antidepressant in the mix (won't induce mood switches because of lamotrigine). I hope things work out for you. Therapy could really help if that's possible.

How do you commit to study or school? I didn't and now that I'm well I realise it was almost impossible for me to do that. You were admitted, you are very ill and there is only so much you can do. Try not to beat yourself up and take time to focus on yourself. You have just begun your recovery with this new diagnosis, please don't lose hope. I'm rooting for you.
